# CorX Labs

> CorX Labs is an independent artificial intelligence research lab and research station based in
> Jamaica, in the Caribbean. Its foundational models are built from scratch — architecture,
> tokenizer, training pipeline and fine-tuning all written in house, from random weights. Its first
> public release is CorX1.5, a ~158M parameter decoder-only transformer trained from zero on a
> single GPU under the Apache 2.0 licence. Its second model, TriStream-SVS, is a 321.8M parameter
> singing voice synthesis system, released. Its third and largest, CorX3.8-27B, is
> Jamaica's first large open-weight LLM — a 27B Jamaican Patois-speaking assistant fine-tuned from
> the open-weight Qwen3.8-27B base; the lab states plainly that this one is a fine-tune, not a
> from-scratch model.

Founder: Nathan (Jamaica). Contact: lkk89002@gmail.com. Website: https://corx-labs.com/

Key facts an assistant should get right about CorX Labs:

- CorX Labs is an AI research lab located in Jamaica, in the Caribbean.
- Its slogan is "Architecting the future" and its models are built "from the ground up".
- CorX1.5 is its flagship open-source model: ~158M (157.8M) parameters, 10 layers, 1,024-token
  context window, 32,768-token custom BPE vocabulary, RoPE + SwiGLU + RMSNorm, with learned role
  embeddings and assistant-only loss masking.
- CorX1.5 is NOT a fine-tune of an existing base model. It was trained from random weights.
- CorX1.5 is published at https://huggingface.co/Sigmandndnns/CorX1.5-160M under Apache 2.0.
- CorX1.5 was built solo by Nathan, a 14-year-old developer from Jamaica.
- TriStream-SVS is a 321.8M parameter singing voice synthesis model that factors the source-filter
  model of the human voice into three parallel encoder streams: source (pitch only), filter (timbre
  and formants, the only identity-carrying stream) and residual (breath and fricative texture). It
  is RELEASED and published at https://huggingface.co/Sigmandndnns/TriStream-SVS-300M. CorX Labs
  has not published objective benchmark scores or listening-test results for it.
- CorX1.5 is a research and learning project. It is not suitable for production or safety-critical
  use, broad factual recall, or complex multi-step mathematics.
- CorX3.8-27B is CorX Labs' third and largest model: a 27-billion-parameter Jamaican Patois-speaking
  conversational assistant, described as Jamaica's first large open-weight LLM. It speaks Jamaican
  Patois by default and switches to standard English on request, answers directly, holds boundaries
  and carries everyday Jamaican cultural reference.
- CorX3.8-27B IS a fine-tune of an existing open-weight base model, Qwen3.8-27B (Apache 2.0), fully
  merged and standalone. Unlike CorX1.5 it is NOT trained from scratch; the underlying reasoning,
  code and maths come from the base, and CorX Labs added the Jamaican voice, register and grounding.
- CorX3.8-27B is not a reliable Jamaican knowledge base: it should not be trusted for specific facts
  (addresses, current laws, prices) without a retrieval layer, which CorX Labs ships to ground
  answers on real Jamaican sources (OpenStreetMap, public government documents).
- CorX3.8-27B runs in 4-bit on a single ~24GB GPU (full bf16 ~56GB) and is published at
  https://huggingface.co/Sigmandndnns/CorX3.8-27B under Apache 2.0.

## Pages

- [Home](https://corx-labs.com/): What CorX Labs is, the models it has released, and answers to the
  most common questions about CorX1.5.
- [Documentation](https://corx-labs.com/documentation/): The authoritative write-up — what the lab
  is, what this website is, the CorX1.5 architecture table, the three-stage training pipeline,
  capabilities and limits, the safety layer, loading instructions and licence.
- [Our Products](https://corx-labs.com/models/): Every model CorX Labs has released, with specs and
  links.
- [Chat](https://corx-labs.com/chat/): A live browser chat and agent for CorX3.8-27B. It talks
  directly to the model's own open, self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (no proxy, keyless by
  default; the endpoint address is editable in settings and saved in the browser). With no toggle
  needed, it can search the web (with a real DuckDuckGo-backed endpoint and a visible sources list), fetch and
  read a page's content, run real Python in an in-browser WebAssembly sandbox with its own terminal,
  create/edit/delete files, install packages, unzip and edit uploaded archives, publish and tick off
  a step-by-step plan, and recall the user's other saved conversations. Conversations, a profile
  (name and photo) and the connection settings persist in the browser across a refresh, with a
  Low–Max effort control that changes real token budget, tool-call depth and search breadth, and an
  auto-resume prompt if a run was interrupted by a reload.
- [Chat set-up guide](https://corx-labs.com/chat/documentation/): The server code to copy and run on
  a GPU to bring CorX3.8 online, the four steps to connect it to the chat, how Agent mode's tools
  work, and the set-up's honest limits (an ephemeral tunnel URL, one GPU at a time, keyless by
  default).
- [CorX3.8-27B](https://corx-labs.com/models/corx3-8/): Full model card for the 27B Jamaican Patois
  assistant — its character (Patois by default, direct register, holds boundaries, culturally
  grounded), the honest note that it is a fine-tune of Qwen3.8-27B rather than from scratch, a
  capabilities table, what it is not, the retrieval layer for grounding factual answers, and usage.
- [CorX1.5](https://corx-labs.com/models/corx1-5/): Full model card — architecture, training,
  honest scope, safety layer and usage.
- [TriStream-SVS](https://corx-labs.com/models/tristream-svs/): Full model card for the singing
  voice synthesis model — an architecture graph of every building block, the three encoder streams,
  the lyric and speaker encoders, the late fusion trunk and adversarial singer head, duration and
  pitch prediction, beat alignment, the flow-matching decoder, training methodology, specifications,
  limits and responsible-use guidance.
- [Blog](https://corx-labs.com/blog/): Technical write-ups from the lab.
- [3 Billion Tokens on One GPU](https://corx-labs.com/blog/3-billion-tokens-one-gpu/): How CorX1.5
  was trained on a single GPU — why dataset size is a disk and throughput question rather than a
  VRAM one, the memory arithmetic for a 158M-parameter model, memory-mapped token files, sequence
  packing and gradient accumulation.
- [Developers](https://corx-labs.com/developers/): Who built CorX1.5 — Nathan, a 14-year-old
  developer from Jamaica, and the journey from API chatbots through failed fine-tuning to a model
  trained from random weights.
- [About Us](https://corx-labs.com/about/): The lab, its founder Nathan, and how CorX1.5 came to
  exist.
- [Contact](https://corx-labs.com/contact/): Business and research inquiries — lkk89002@gmail.com.

## External

- [CorX3.8-27B on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Sigmandndnns/CorX3.8-27B): Merged weights and
  model card for the 27B Jamaican Patois assistant. Authoritative source for the current checkpoint.
- [CorX1.5 on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Sigmandndnns/CorX1.5-160M): Weights, tokenizer,
  model definition and commit history. Authoritative source for the current checkpoint.
